items.note: Policy note 'Parkeren in Oss 2025' (PDF, 30 pages, read in full). Colophon: 'Datum vaststelling gemeenteraad: 26 mei 2025', 'Datum publicatie 11 juni 2025'. Ch. 5: bundle car parking in built facilities at the edge of the centre; long-stay visitors to Bergoss and Oostwal garages (west/south route), Burchtplein (north, 'meer sturen op lang-parkeren') and a Raadhuislaan facility; paid hours extended to 22:00; more room for pedestrians, cyclists and greenery. All claims match.

Same policy note, p. 27 tariff table: first 30 min EUR 1 then EUR 4/h on the 'zeer kort parkeren' streets; other centre streets plus fringe districts EUR 2 first hour then EUR 4/h; Bergoss, Oostwal-Oost, Burchtplein, Raadhuishof EUR 2/h with EUR 6 day rate; resident permits EUR 75 / EUR 150; subscriptions EUR 450 night, EUR 600 office hours, EUR 900 24/7. Every number matches. (The note also lists other lots at EUR 2/h, not mentioned; the structure was later replaced by the 2026-II ordinance, see item 9.)

Policy note p. 26 and p. 28: costs and revenues of paid parking, permit parking and guarded bicycle parking 'sinds 1994 samengebracht in het Parkeerbedrijf', closed account, must be cost-covering. P. 28: 'Het straatparkeren en parkeerterrein Jurgensplein zijn financieel rendabel. Deze dekken de kosten van de financieel onrendabele activiteiten zoals fietsparkeren, parkeergarage Oostwal-Oost en parkeergarage Bergoss.' The note says costs of the garages sit in the Parkeerbedrijf account; operation is shown in item 12. Matches.

Policy note p. 18: 'op gemiddelde werkdagen ruim voldoende parkeerplaatsen', highest pressure on Saturdays and during events, Jurgensplein, Boschpoorthof and Eikenboomgaard intensively used, Bergoss and Oostwal-Oost 'nagenoeg altijd parkeerplaatsen beschikbaar' except during the kermis, evening pressure rising due to hospitality visits. All as in the text. Appendix 1 with actual occupancy data is not in the PDF, so these are the municipality's general statements, as the item says.

Omroep Brabant article is dated 2 September 2025 (modified 7 Oct 2025) and is written BEFORE the change: 'De gemeente verandert vanaf 1 oktober het parkeerbeleid', 'worden hoger', 'wordt ... tot tien uur'. The draft states as completed fact that Oss raised the costs. The numbers are right (stays over half an hour, garage day rate from 4 to 6 euros, paid parking until 22:00 instead of 18:00, municipality's reasons). 'More than 200' is 'meer dan tweehonderd Ossenaren' reacting under the announcement of Weekblad Regio Oss; the page does not say 'on social media'. That the policy took effect on 1 October 2025 is confirmed by the CMO report (item 6), not by this page.
items.corrected_text: Omroep Brabant reported on 2 September 2025 that from 1 October 2025 the municipality would change its parking policy: parking would cost more for people leaving their car in or around the centre for longer than half an hour, the day rate in the garages would rise from 4 to 6 euros, and paid parking would run until 22:00 instead of 18:00. The municipality said this would make room for cyclists, pedestrians and greenery. More than 200 residents reacted indignantly under the announcement by Weekblad Regio Oss.

items.note: Omroep Brabant, 10 October 2025 (modified 18 Oct): alderman Van den Bergh announced on the Thursday evening (9 Oct) a maximum of EUR 12 per day 'per 1 november' on Eikenboomgaardplein, Boschpoorthof, Oostwal, Kruisstraat, Maasvallei, Lievekamplaan, Ridderhof, Spoorlaan and Jurgensplein; goes to B&W and 'zou op 23 oktober al door de gemeenteraad vastgesteld kunnen worden'; EUR 6 day rate already applies at Bergoss, the garage on the Oostwal, Burchtplein and behind the town hall; real evaluation end of 2026. Item words it as announced and pending. Matches. Outcome of the 23 October vote not on the page.

CMO report of the 20 October 2025 meeting (PDF, 4 pages, read in full), written by the centre manager on 21 Oct 2025: 15.4% fall from 1,594 (2022) to 1,349 'nu', including 'de 200 plaatsen aan de Maasvallei ... achter een hek'; Burchtplein 253 places, a considerable share taken by permit holders; Oostwal Oost 142 places; Sept 2023 study 'Relatie Mobiliteit en Bestedingen': car 37% of visitors, 55% of turnover. All numbers match. The page never calls the CMO a 'foundation' and never says it 'represents' traders (item 7's article says the centre management did not back the petition), so that wording is dropped. Figures are the CMO's own, as the item says.
items.corrected_text: The centre management organisation (CMO), reporting on a meeting with centre traders on 20 October 2025, said that the number of central parking spaces fell by 15.4 percent from 1,594 in 2022 to 1,349 in October 2025, including about 200 spaces at Maasvallei lying unused behind a fence. It put Burchtplein at 253 spaces (a considerable share taken by permit holders) and Oostwal-Oost at 142 spaces, and cited a September 2023 study in which cars made up 37 percent of visitors but 55 percent of turnover. This is the CMO's own account, not an official count.

items.note: Omroep Brabant 'Ondernemers starten handtekeningenactie tegen parkeertarief: Omzet omlaag'. Year: the visible page shows only '23 januari', but the page's own metadata (datePublished/publicationDate) reads 2026-01-23, and the text refers to the 1 October change and 'de laatste drie maanden van het jaar', so 2026 is verified. Content: chocolatier 'achttien procent omzet misgelopen' in the last three months, 'runshoppers' quote from a clothing shop owner, centre management does not support the action, action runs 'tot begin maart'. But the article (a Friday) says traders 'starten dinsdag' (will start on Tuesday), so 'launched' is too strong.
items.corrected_text: Omroep Brabant reported on 23 January 2026 that centre traders were to start a signature campaign on the following Tuesday against the higher tariffs and longer paid hours, running until early March. One chocolatier said he lost 18 percent of turnover in the last three months of the year, and a clothing retailer said shoppers had become 'runshoppers' instead of 'funshoppers'. The centre management did not support the action. These are traders' statements.
items.corrected_title: Ondernemers starten handtekeningenactie tegen parkeertarief (Omroep Brabant, 23 January 2026)

items.note: Omroep Brabant 3 June 'Parkeren centrum Oss wordt weer goedkoper na maanden kritiek'. Content matches: paid parking to end at 20:00 instead of 22:00; EUR 2/h on streets everywhere; EUR 6 day maximum for lots and garages; from 1 October if the council agrees at the end of the month; alderman: 'Voorlopig gaan we het niet meer hebben over parkeertarieven'. Year: not in the visible text, but the page's own metadata (datePublished 2026-06-03T13:50Z) says 2026, and it matches the ordinance of 25 June 2026 (item 9). The draft's hedge 'year not printed on the page' is therefore unnecessary; text corrected.
items.corrected_text: Omroep Brabant reported on 3 June 2026 that the municipality proposed to partly reverse the increase: paid parking would end at 20:00 instead of 22:00, streets would all cost 2 euros per hour, and lots and garages would get a maximum of 6 euros per day, starting 1 October if the council agreed at the end of the month. The alderman said tariffs would not be discussed again for now.
items.corrected_title: Parkeren centrum Oss wordt weer goedkoper na maanden kritiek (Omroep Brabant, 3 June 2026)

items.note: CVDR764532 (text read in full). Intro: council, proposal of 2 June 2026; closing: 'openbare raadsvergadering van 25 juni 2026'; Art. 14: in force 1 October 2026 (page: 'Geldend van 01-10-2026 t/m heden'). Annex 1: paid times Mon-Sat 09:00-20:00, not on listed legal holidays; B1 lots (Eikenboomgaardplein, Boschpoorthof, Oostwal-West, Kruisstraat, Maasvallei, Lievekamplaan, Ridderhof, Spoorlaan, Burchtplein, Raadhuishof) EUR 2/h with EUR 6 day maximum; A1 listed streets EUR 2/h; D1 all other locations in centre and fringe zones EUR 2 first hour then EUR 4/h; resident permit EUR 75, second EUR 150. All numbers match; 'valid from 1 October 2026' is stated by the text. (The ordinance also sets EUR 150 for a resident who has own-site parking; not mentioned in item.)

CVDR764533 (read in full). 'Oss, 7 juli 2026' signed by the college; Art. 18: in force 1 October 2026. Art. 4 table: zone A 247 spaces / 190 permits, zone B 406 / 230, zone C 423 / 20. Table 1: zones A and B 'Maximaal 1 per adres, mits geen parkeren op eigen terrein'. All numbers match. But the zones are A to H plus J (there is no zone I), so 'zones A to J' suggests ten zones. Zone C gets no resident permits (business permits only), which explains the low cap.
items.corrected_text: The Uitwerkingsbesluit Parkeren Oss en Ravenstein 2026 (signed by the municipal executive on 7 July 2026, in force from 1 October 2026) sets permit zones around the centre (zones A to H and J, plus separate Ravenstein zones) and a cap on permits per zone, for example zone A 190 permits for 247 spaces, zone B 230 for 406 and zone C only 20 for 423 spaces (zone C is for business permits only). Residents in centre zones A and B can get at most one permit per address, and only without private parking.

items.note: Municipal page 'Nieuwe parkeertarieven vanaf 1 oktober 2026' (undated; read 21 Oct 2026). Matches: most spaces paid 09:00-20:00, free on Sundays and official holidays; garages Bergoss (Oostwal 177) and Oostwal-Oost (Oostwal 241) paid 24/7 also on holidays; garages and lots EUR 2/h, max EUR 6 per day; shopping streets EUR 2/h no daily maximum; Rusheuvel stays free. 'Scan car' is NOT on this page: it only says parking is by licence plate and enforcers check the plate (the scan car appears only in the policy note). Dropped. The page also lists residential areas at EUR 2 first hour then EUR 4/h and Jurgensplein as pay-afterwards.
items.corrected_text: The municipal tariff page (read on 21 October 2026) states that from 1 October 2026 most parking spaces in and around the centre are paid 09:00-20:00 and free on Sundays and official holidays, while the garages (Bergoss, Oostwal 177; Oostwal-Oost, Oostwal 241) charge 24 hours a day, every day, also on holidays. Garages and lots (including Jurgensplein, where payment is made afterwards) cost 2 euros per hour up to 6 euros per day, shopping streets 2 euros per hour with no day maximum, and in some residential areas around the centre 2 euros for the first hour and then 4 euros per hour. The Rusheuvel lot north of the centre stays free. Parking is by licence plate, with no ticket.

items.note: Beheerplan Parkeren 2021-2022 (September 2021, printed 16-12-2021, read in full). Activities list the Jurgensplein lot, the Oostwal Oost deck and the Bergoss garage; 2.7.3: Bergoss 'sinds september 2009 geopend'; 2.7.2: Oostwal Oost 'in gedeelde eigendom met ImmoPartners Beheer'; operational management of Bergoss by IBN 'circa EUR 0,2 miljoen per jaar'; proposed shorter opening hours (69 instead of 90 occupancy hours/week), 'potentiele bezuiniging van circa EUR 45.000 per jaar'. All as stated; worded as a proposal.

Policy note p. 26 (financial premises): 'Voor de parkeervoorziening aan Raadhuislaan-zuid gaan we uit van de realisatie van een integrale parkeeroplossing op het huidige parkeerterrein achter het gemeentehuis en De Lievekamp (conform scenario 2 uit de opinienota, ... commissie Ruimte d.d. 21 november 2024). Een openbare, bovengrondse parkeervoorziening parallel aan de spoorlijn met een capaciteit van afgerond 700 parkeerplaatsen.' So 700 is a rounded planning assumption for the note's calculations, not a decided design; 'provides for' is slightly too strong. P. 16: multi-function (theatre, city-centre visitors, living, working); p. 28: co-invest in and operate a built facility at Raadhuislaan. Burchtplein 'op de langere termijn zou ... kunnen transformeren'; Koornstraat lot 'bouwen we om' to a bicycle facility. Rest matches.
items.corrected_text: The 2025 policy note assumes, for its financial calculations, a public above-ground garage of a rounded 700 spaces parallel to the railway on the current lot behind the town hall and De Lievekamp (Raadhuislaan-zuid; scenario 2 of an options paper discussed in a council committee on 21 November 2024). It describes the facility as a shared one for the theatre, city-centre visitors, residents and workers, which the municipality plans to co-invest in and operate. In the longer term the Burchtplein lot could become a built facility, and the Koornstraat lot is to be converted into guarded bicycle parking. These are plans, not completed projects.

items.note: Omroep Brabant 3 June (2026 per page metadata, see item 8): lower parking revenue means a guarded bicycle garage at Eikenboomgaard is 'voorlopig van de baan', improvements to garage Oostwal-Oost 'worden uitgesteld', a future lot at Burchtplein 'in de ijskast'; financing of the new Raadhuiskwartier garage 'blijft een uitdaging ... nog een oplossing worden gevonden'; for the Lievekamp expansion, a new parking garage, Rabobank tower, and redesign of Raadhuislaan and Lievekamplaan 'afspraken gemaakt over de financiering'. All as stated; these follow from a proposal still awaiting the council. Year 2026 verified from page metadata.
items.corrected_title: Parkeren centrum Oss wordt weer goedkoper na maanden kritiek (Omroep Brabant, 3 June 2026)

items.note: Policy note ch. 6 (pp. 22-24): station Oss to be upgraded as a central regional mobility hub (train, Bus Rapid Transit, bus, bike, shared mobility); Nota Parkeernormen Oss 2023 (October 2023) with lower norms in the Spoorzone; option of proactive paid parking with permits in a 'potentieel gereguleerd parkeergebied' wider than the Spoorzone, and future residents/users of the developments 'gaan niet in aanmerking komen voor eventuele parkeervergunningen'. Worded as foreseen/option. Matches.

Q-Park page 'Parkeren bij Q-Park P+R Gasstraat' (read 21 Oct 2026, undated live page): Gasstraat, 5349 AV Oss; Parkeerplaatsen 246; Doorrijhoogte 2.10 m; opening Mon-Sun 24-7; services Kentekenherkenning, Fietsenstalling, Mindervalideplekken, OV Knooppunt; traveller discount if checking in and out at different stations and leaving the same day as the return train trip; 'De tarieven konden helaas niet geladen worden'. All as stated. Note: the page's embedded data lists 0 bicycle and 0 disabled spaces while the service list names both; the item follows the visible service list.

Municipal charging vision 2024-2030 (PDF read in full; the oss.nl URL redirects to www.oss.nl). Summary: 'stelt de gemeente Oss dat er 1.365 openbare laadpunten nodig zijn ... stijging van ca 400% ten opzichte van het huidige aantal van 340'; forecast 'ongeveer 13.573' electric vehicles in 2030. Fast chargers: 'Deze plaatsen we als gemeente niet in de openbare ruimte' (ch. 8.2: 'in principe' not on municipal land). But Vattenfall: rollout 'van 2020 tot 2024 belegd bij Vattenfall' under the joint Noord-Brabant/Limburg concession, with a new collective tender for a concession starting July 2024 in preparation; the item states in the present tense that Vattenfall provides the services. Also note the document's own ElaadNL forecast chart (p. 16) shows about 1,937 public points by 2030, so 1,365 is the summary figure only.
items.corrected_text: The municipal charging vision 2024-2030 states that Oss needs 1,365 public charging points by 2030 against about 340 at the time of writing, for an expected 13,573 electric vehicles. It says the rollout of public charge points was assigned to Vattenfall under a joint Noord-Brabant and Limburg concession for 2020-2024, with a new joint concession being prepared to start in July 2024. The municipality does not place fast chargers in public space and in principle leaves them to the market.

corrected_summary: Oss (about 95,000 inhabitants) has a municipal, cost-covering parking company (Parkeerbedrijf) whose accounts include the Bergoss and Oostwal-Oost garages and the Jurgensplein lot; in 2021 it ran them with outside operational management. On 26 May 2025 the council adopted the policy note 'Parkeren in Oss 2025': bundle long-stay parking in built facilities at the edge of the centre, give pedestrians, cyclists and greenery more room, add free guarded bicycle parking, and raise tariffs and paid hours to fund new facilities. The new tariffs, announced in September 2025 to apply from 1 October 2025 (paid parking until 22:00, garage day rate from 4 to 6 euros), met strong protest from residents and traders; in October 2025 the alderman announced a 12-euro day cap on surface lots from 1 November 2025, subject to council approval. In June 2026 the municipality proposed a softer scheme, and the council adopted the ordinance on 25 June 2026: from 1 October 2026 paid parking runs Monday to Saturday 09:00-20:00, lots and garages cost 2 euros per hour with a 6-euro day maximum, and shopping streets cost 2 euros per hour, according to the municipal tariff page read on 21 October 2026. The 2025 note assumes a public garage of about 700 spaces on the Raadhuislaan next to the railway line, but in June 2026 its financing was still described as unresolved, and several smaller projects (a guarded bicycle garage at Eikenboomgaard, upgrades to Oostwal-Oost, a Burchtplein facility) were postponed. The centre management organisation reports fewer central spaces (1,594 in 2022 to 1,349 in October 2025), while the municipality's own note finds spare capacity on normal weekdays and peaks on Saturdays and during events. Station parking is separate: Q-Park runs P+R Gasstraat (246 spaces; tariffs could not be read), and the policy note aims to upgrade Station Oss as a mobility hub with lower parking norms in the Spoorzone. The 2024 charging vision says Oss needs 1,365 public charging points by 2030 against about 340 then.
